subject: Minimum inflight throughput amendment request — Nimbus Data Dedicated Pool
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@nimbusdata.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nimbusdata.com
Date: 2028-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: minimum inflight throughput guarantee for Dedicated pool

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Dedicated pool performance looked very promising. Before we move to LOI, legal and infra have one open ask: can Redwood commit to a minimum inflight throughput (requests-in-flight) guarantee during our peak window? Specifically: Nimbus needs a guarantee that at 98th percentile we will have at least 120 concurrent inference inflight tokens/sec capacity reserved to avoid request tail latencies impacting our SLA to end customers.

This is different from your per-GPU reservation language — we need a behavioral guarantee (minimum usable concurrency for short peaks) and clarity on queueing/backpressure behavior when demand briefly exceeds the reservation. A few practical questions:
- Will Redwood expose a blocking vs. queuing policy we can rely on?
- If you use burst capacity or fallback pools, can you guarantee failover latency under 500ms for establishing new worker leases?
- Can we get a runbook for how Redwood measures and credits throughput shortfalls (credits, rollback, or headroom)?

I attached a short throughput report from our PoC (Throughput_Report_20280620.csv) showing the peak profile. Procurement copied to align on commercial language.

Best,
Samir
Samir Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
Nimbus Data

From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@nimbusdata.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@nimbusdata.com
Date: 2028-06-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: minimum inflight throughput guarantee for Dedicated pool

Samir — thanks for the clear note and the PoC CSV. We can absolutely discuss an operational addendum that maps to your "minimum usable concurrency" ask. A few immediate clarifications so we scope this correctly:

1) When you say "120 concurrent inference inflight tokens/sec capacity" — do you mean 120 concurrent requests (RPS) with your typical request size (avg token length ~80), or 120 token/sec aggregate? The mitigation approach differs.

2) Are you open to a two-tier guarantee: (A) a firm per-hour reservation (GPU-backed) that maps to a defined sustainable concurrency, and (B) a documented short-duration headroom (burst) policy with measurable fallbacks and crediting? That lets us preserve deterministic throughput for your core window and provide controlled burst for unexpected spikes.

Ben and Laura — I’m looping you for technical and contractual detail. I can produce an initial SLA amendment draft for Nimbus that defines measurement windows, how we compute the 98th percentile, and crediting formulas. Would Nimbus procurement accept an addendum that:
- defines the per-hour reserved throughput baseline
- includes a 10-minute rolling headroom policy (with explicit preemption/queueing semantics)
- guarantees failover lease establishment < 500ms for cold-starts within the same region, and < 2s if cross-region fallback is used

If that sounds acceptable I’ll send a redline. Next steps: I’ll draft a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and attach the proposed legal addendum.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@nimbusdata.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-21T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: minimum inflight throughput guarantee for Dedicated pool

Samir — quick technical note from runtime team:

- We typically express capacity as concurrent request slots (inflight requests) rather than tokens/sec. With your avg request size (~80 tokens) and our model config, 120 concurrent requests aligns with ~9-12 dedicated V100-equivalent slots depending on quantization.
- Queueing behavior: by default we allow a short in-memory FIFO queue per tenant up to N requests (configurable). Beyond that, requests receive 429 backpressure. For dedicated customers we can change the policy to strictly reserve X inflight slots and route overflow to a bounded queue prioritized by token-age and tenant-criticality.
- Headroom/burst: we can provide a 10-minute burst window backed by pre-warmed warm-workers; failover to regional fallback will incur ~600-800ms on first lease in our tests, so Naomi's <500ms guarantee is aggressive cross-region but achievable intra-region for pre-warmed capacity.

If Nimbus wants a hard guarantee at 98th on inflight slots, we'll define a mapping from "reserved GPUs" to "reserved inflight slots" and include an explicit measurement method (rolling windows, telemetry endpoints, and audit logs).

I can prepare the technical appendix for the SLA addendum.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Systems Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@nimbusdata.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@nimbusdata.com>, procurement@nimbusdata.com
Date: 2028-06-22T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Nimbus: redlines to SLA addendum draft attached

Naomi, Ben — attaching our procurement redlines (Nimbus_SLA_Redline_v3.pdf). High level: procurement wants the inflight guarantee written as a behavioral SLA ("98th percentile usable concurrency >= 120 inflight requests over 1-hour windows") with explicit crediting tied to monthly invoices. They also want a clause that prevents Redwood from relying on cross-region fallback to meet the guarantee during the reserved window unless pre-approved.

A few negotiation bullets we flagged:
- Measurement: we prefer an external telemetry feed (push) to Nimbus with 1s granularity for the peak windows for visibility.
- Credits: pro-rated monthly credit (2x the token cost for each minute of shortfall beyond 5 minutes per month) — see redline.
- Emergency escalation: a 15-minute response SLA for infrastructure escalation during severe throughput shortfalls.

Please confirm receipt and next steps. Our legal can take a look in parallel.

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Procurement Manager
Nimbus Data

From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@nimbusdata.com>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@nimbusdata.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-23T17:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus: redlines to SLA addendum draft attached

Alicia — got your redlines, thanks. Internal notes and proposed path forward below: 

1) Measurement & telemetry: Redwood can publish a push telemetry feed for the reserved window; we will provide 1s-resolution inflight slot metrics and a daily digest during ramp. We'll include a signed SLA appendix that specifies the measurement endpoints and a mutually agreed sampling scheme.

2) Cross-region fallback: we agree to a contractual restriction that cross-region fallback cannot be used to meet the reserved-window guarantee unless Nimbus explicitly authorizes it for that window. In that case we will document expected additional failover latencies in the appendix.

3) Crediting: your proposed pro-rated monthly credit is reasonable but we prefer a tiered credit (smaller credits for short interruptions, escalated credits for repeated or prolonged shortfalls). Ben, Laura — I'll ask you to propose the detailed credit tiers and a simple example calculation for the next draft.

4) Escalation: we can commit to a 15-minute acknowledgement for production-impacting throughput incidents with a 60-minute remediation checkpoint. We'll include contact rotation in the MAP.

Next steps: I will circulate a redlined addendum (legal + tech appendix) by EOD Monday, including concrete definitions (what constitutes an "inflight request", sample queries to compute the 98th percentile, and the crediting math). If Nimbus procurement is happy with the tiers we can move to a signature-ready addendum and attach it to the LOI.

Thanks everyone — appreciate the pragmatic suggestions.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
